about: Message Center posts with PowerShell for the FEATURE itself (find where it is used, use it, move off it) - not only for reading the post. Written by hand or by the morning routine (routines/poranny-B-publish.md STEP -1d), checked by tools/mc_howto_todo.py check: every block parses, every Graph cmdlet and parameter exists in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK, scopes are named, writes carry -WhatIf. A post without a note shows nothing; `scriptable: false` says why no script exists. Author: Piotr Wisniewski.

notes.title: MemberOf rule operator in dynamic groups, dynamic administrative units and auto-assignment policies
notes.dates: 03/11/2026 - the preview ends: configurations that use memberOf stop updating and keep their last membership (MC1448379, MC1488834, MC1529463; Learn). Tenants with Microsoft Entra ID Governance or higher: existing configurations keep working until 31/03/2027, then Microsoft migrates them to a new MemberOf capability (MC1488839, published 05/10/2026). On 03/11/2026 the Learn pages still give only 03/11/2026 and do not mention the extension.

blocks.t: Find dynamic groups that use memberOf
blocks.code:
# Read only. Lists every dynamic group whose rule uses memberOf (a memberOf rule cannot be combined with other conditions).
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'GroupMember.Read.All' -NoWelcome
$groups = Get-MgGroup -Filter "groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'DynamicMembership')" -All `
    -Property Id, DisplayName, MembershipRule, MembershipRuleProcessingState
$memberOf = $groups | Where-Object { $_.MembershipRule -match '(?i)memberof' }
$memberOf | Select-Object DisplayName, Id, MembershipRuleProcessingState, MembershipRule |
    Export-Csv -Path .\memberof-dynamic-groups.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
"{0} of {1} dynamic groups use memberOf" -f @($memberOf).Count, @($groups).Count

blocks.t: Find dynamic administrative units that use memberOf
blocks.code:
# Read only. The filter runs on your computer, so no advanced query is needed.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'AdministrativeUnit.Read.All' -NoWelcome
Get-MgDirectoryAdministrativeUnit -All -Property Id, DisplayName, MembershipType, MembershipRule, MembershipRuleProcessingState |
    Where-Object { $_.MembershipType -eq 'Dynamic' -and $_.MembershipRule -match '(?i)memberof' } |
    Select-Object DisplayName, Id, MembershipRuleProcessingState, MembershipRule

blocks.t: Find auto-assignment policies (access packages) that use memberOf
Keep a record of who is in each group before the date
How the feature is used: a memberOf group (test tenant only)
blocks.warn: The operator is a retiring preview: do not build new production groups on it. -WhatIf shows what would be created; remove it only in a test tenant.
blocks.code:
# WRITE - test tenant only. Members of the source group(s) become members of the new dynamic group.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Group.ReadWrite.All' -NoWelcome
$source = '<object id of the source group>'
New-MgGroup -DisplayName 'DYN - members of Sales (memberOf test)' -MailNickname 'dyn-memberof-test' `
    -MailEnabled:$false -SecurityEnabled -GroupTypes 'DynamicMembership' `
    -MembershipRule "user.memberof -any (group.objectId -in ['$source'])" `
    -MembershipRuleProcessingState 'On' -WhatIf

blocks.t: Move off it: rebuild the rule with an attribute, or make the group assigned
blocks.warn: Changes membership. Run with -WhatIf first, on one group, and compare the members with the CSV of the previous block.
blocks.code:
# WRITE. Option A - the source group's members share an attribute: replace the rule (here: department).
Update-MgGroup -GroupId '<group id>' -MembershipRule '(user.department -eq "Sales")' -MembershipRuleProcessingState 'On' -WhatIf

# Option B - no attribute fits: make the group assigned (Microsoft's way on Learn: drop only 'DynamicMembership', keep 'Unified').
# Its current members stay; from now on you add and remove them yourself.
$groupId = '<group id>'
$types = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]@((Get-MgGroup -GroupId $groupId -Property GroupTypes).GroupTypes)
[void]$types.Remove('DynamicMembership')
Update-MgGroup -GroupId $groupId -GroupTypes $types.ToArray() -MembershipRuleProcessingState 'Paused' -WhatIf

sources.t: Microsoft Learn: memberOf operator (preview) - migrate before the preview ends
sources.says: After 3 November 2026 dynamic groups, dynamic administrative units and auto-assignment policies that use memberOf stop updating and keep their last state; lists the preview limits (500 groups, 50 source groups, no other conditions).

notes.title: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire for self-service password reset (SSPR)

blocks.t: Find SSPR-registered users whose only registered methods are phone numbers
blocks.code:
# Read only. Lists users registered for SSPR whose registered methods are all phone-based,
# i.e. the users who lose self-service recovery when Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'AuditLog.Read.All' -NoWelcome
$phone = @('mobilePhone','alternateMobilePhone','officePhone')
$details = Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail -All -Filter 'isSsprRegistered eq true'
$atRisk = $details | Where-Object {
    $m = @($_.MethodsRegistered)
    $m.Count -gt 0 -and -not ($m | Where-Object { $_ -notin $phone })
}
$atRisk | Select-Object UserPrincipalName, UserDisplayName, @{n='Methods';e={$_.MethodsRegistered -join ','}} |
    Export-Csv -Path .\sspr-phone-only-users.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
"{0} of {1} SSPR-registered users have only phone methods" -f @($atRisk).Count, @($details).Count

notes.dates: MC1536049 (3 November 2026): SMS/voice sign-in retirement rollout begins 1 February 2027 for most users and 1 July 2027 for Global Administrators and external users; each population keeps Microsoft-provided SMS/voice for SSPR for 50 days after its rollout reaches the tenant. Action-required date shown by DeltaPulse: 22 March 2027.

sources.says: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice stop being usable for SSPR 50 days after the SMS/voice sign-in retirement reaches each population; customer-managed telephony remains available and Microsoft will not change the SSPR policy automatically.

Documents the report with isSsprRegistered and methodsRegistered filters, least privileged permission AuditLog.Read.All, and the PowerShell cmdlet Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail.

notes.title: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing move from EWS to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy
notes.dates: Free/Busy and MailTips through Cross-Tenant Access Policy by 15/09/2026, calendar sharing by 06/11/2026 (previously 30/10/2026); EWS is disabled gradually from 01/10/2026 and switched off finally on 01/04/2027 (MC1446796, updated 30/10/2026). Government clouds are paused.

blocks.t: Is the tenant affected? Organization relationships that share Free/Busy or MailTips
blocks.scopes: Exchange Online: a role that can run Get-OrganizationRelationship (for example View-Only Organization Management)
blocks.code:
# Read only. Microsoft's own check from MC1446796.
Connect-ExchangeOnline
Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScope
# Affected when Enabled is True, FreeBusyAccessEnabled or MailTipsAccessEnabled is True, and the partner is hosted in Microsoft 365.

blocks.t: Is the tenant affected? Sharing policies with calendar sharing rules
blocks.scopes: Exchange Online: a role that can run Get-SharingPolicy (for example View-Only Organization Management)
blocks.code:
# Read only. Microsoft's own check from MC1446796.
Connect-ExchangeOnline
Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, Default
# Affected when Enabled is True, Domains holds a CalendarSharingFreeBusy rule (Simple, Detail or Reviewer) for a Microsoft 365 partner,
# and the policy is assigned to mailboxes. Rules starting with Anonymous: are calendars published to an internet URL.

sources.says: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing that rely on EWS move to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy; calendar sharing is available by 6 November 2026, and the post gives the two Exchange Online PowerShell checks used here.

notes.title: Outlook for Windows usage report leaves the Exchange admin center (early April 2027)
notes.dates: Revised 06/11/2026: retirement begins and completes in early April 2027 (previously early November 2026). No admin action required; the same data stays in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 Apps.

blocks.t: Read Outlook for Windows usage per user from the Microsoft 365 Apps usage report
blocks.code:
# Read only. The Microsoft 365 Apps user detail report carries an 'Outlook (Windows)' column - the data the EAC report showed.
# Delegated use also needs a Microsoft Entra role allowed to read usage reports (for example Reports Reader).
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Reports.Read.All' -NoWelcome
Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET `
    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/reports/getM365AppUserDetail(period='D30')?`$format=text/csv" `
    -OutputFilePath .\m365-apps-user-detail-D30.csv
$rows = Import-Csv .\m365-apps-user-detail-D30.csv
$rows | Where-Object { $_.'Outlook (Windows)' -eq 'Yes' } |
    Select-Object 'User Principal Name', 'Last Activity Date', 'Outlook (Windows)' |
    Export-Csv .\outlook-windows-users.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8

sources.says: The Outlook for Windows Usage Report is removed from the Exchange admin center in early April 2027 (moved on 6 November 2026 from early November 2026); usage stays available in the Microsoft 365 admin center; no admin action is required.
Returns per-user Microsoft 365 Apps usage, including an 'Outlook (Windows)' column, with Reports.Read.All as the least privileged permission.

notes.title: Exchange Online Admin API v2.0: find apps that still use Exchange.ManageV2 or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2
notes.dates: Worldwide: the new permissions Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage and Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp are available from 01/11/2026, migration is due by 30/11/2026 and the old ones are deprecated on 01/12/2026; GCC, GCC High and DoD on 01/01/2027 (MC1540345). On 08/11/2026 the Learn authentication page still names only Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2.

blocks.t: Find apps that hold the retiring Admin API permissions
blocks.code:
# Read only. Lists every app that holds the Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 permissions retiring on 1 December 2026.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Application.Read.All','DelegatedPermissionGrant.Read.All' -NoWelcome
$exo = Get-MgServicePrincipal -Filter "displayName eq 'Office 365 Exchange Online'" -Property Id, DisplayName, AppRoles
# App-only: Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 granted as an application permission
$oldRole = $exo.AppRoles | Where-Object { $_.Value -eq 'Exchange.ManageAsAppV2' }
Get-MgServicePrincipalAppRoleAssignedTo -ServicePrincipalId $exo.Id -All |
    Where-Object { $_.AppRoleId -in $oldRole.Id } |
    Select-Object PrincipalDisplayName, PrincipalId, CreatedDateTime
# Delegated: Exchange.ManageV2 in an OAuth2 permission grant
Get-MgOauth2PermissionGrant -Filter "resourceId eq '$($exo.Id)'" -All |
    Where-Object { ($_.Scope -split ' ') -contains 'Exchange.ManageV2' } |
    Select-Object ClientId, ConsentType, PrincipalId, Scope

sources.t: Message Center MC1540345: Update permissions for Exchange Online Admin API
sources.says: Exchange.ManageV2 is replaced by Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 by Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp; the endpoints do not change, apps need the new permission, admin consent and their existing Exchange RBAC roles, and the old permissions are removed after testing.

sources.t: Microsoft Learn: Authentication and authorization for the Exchange Online Admin API
sources.says: The Admin API authentication page (preview) registers the app on Office 365 Exchange Online with Exchange.ManageV2 (delegated) or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 (application) and requires Exchange RBAC roles; a valid token without them fails with 403.

notes.title: Prepare users who can't use passkeys for the Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retirement
notes.dates: 01/02/2027 - Microsoft-provided SMS and voice stop completing MFA for non-admin users (rollout start); 01/07/2027 for Global Administrators and external users (MC1540327, published 05/11/2026).

blocks.t: Find users whose only MFA methods are SMS or voice
blocks.code:
# Read only. Lists users whose ONLY registered MFA methods are phone methods (SMS / voice).
# They need another method (Authenticator push, passwordless phone sign-in or a TOTP code) before the
# Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retirement reaches the tenant (from 1 February 2027; Global Administrators
# and external users from 1 July 2027).
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'AuditLog.Read.All' -NoWelcome
$phone = '^(mobilePhone|alternateMobilePhone|officePhone)$'
$rows = Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail -All `
    -Property UserPrincipalName, UserDisplayName, MethodsRegistered, IsMfaRegistered, IsAdmin
$phoneOnly = $rows | Where-Object {
    $m = @($_.MethodsRegistered)
    $m.Count -gt 0 -and @($m | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch $phone }).Count -eq 0
}
$phoneOnly | Select-Object UserPrincipalName, UserDisplayName, IsAdmin, @{n='Methods';e={$_.MethodsRegistered -join ', '}} |
    Export-Csv -Path .\phone-only-mfa-users.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
"{0} of {1} users have only phone methods registered" -f @($phoneOnly).Count, @($rows).Count

sources.says: Users whose only MFA methods are SMS or voice and who sign in where passkeys are not supported will be blocked once Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire (from 1 February 2027; 1 July 2027 for Global Administrators and external users); admins should register Authenticator push, passwordless phone sign-in or TOTP for them, or set up a customer-managed telephony provider.

The authentication methods registration report lists each user's methodsRegistered; least privileged permission AuditLog.Read.All; PowerShell cmdlet Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail.
Microsoft's page on the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice, linked from the post.

notes.title: Teams device management moves from the Teams admin center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal
notes.dates: Public cloud: SIP, Teams Rooms on Android and panels leave the Teams admin center from mid-November to end of November 2026; phones from early December to 15 December 2026 (MC1448373, updated 29 October 2026). GCC-High and DoD by 15 December 2026, GCC by 30 January 2027.

blocks.t: List the Teams devices the Teams admin center still manages, by type and health
blocks.code:
# Read only. Inventory of Teams devices (phones, Teams Rooms on Android, panels, SIP) as the Teams admin center sees them,
# so you can check each one appears and is manageable in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal before the cut-over.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'TeamworkDevice.Read.All' -NoWelcome
$devices = Get-MgBetaTeamworkDevice -All
$devices | Group-Object DeviceType | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Name, Count
$devices | Select-Object Id, DeviceType, HealthStatus, ActivityState, @{n='Model';e={$_.HardwareDetail.Model}} |
  Export-Csv -Path .\teams-devices-before-pmp.csv -NoTypeInformation

sources.says: Teams admin center device management is deprecated in phases from mid-November 2026; admins should verify every Teams Android device is visible and manageable in the Pro Management portal, update the Admin Agent and bring offline devices online.
Lists Teams devices in the tenant through Microsoft Graph beta; least privileged permission TeamworkDevice.Read.All (delegated and application).
